reason: The lane-born stars are approaching the returning galaxy, so its stellar outskirts are the natural place to follow them.

choice.combine: Young stars from the dark lane
choice.with: Stellar outskirts of the returning galaxy

expectation: The stars will pass through the returning galaxy's outskirts and their paths may change.

effect: The lane-born stars passed through the returning galaxy, their paths changing without the cloud-like collision I had expected them to avoid. The chapter's goal is complete.
reaction: The contrast between the stars crossing and their parent clouds colliding was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Sending the lane-born stars through the returning galaxy brought their story back to the original collision and showed how becoming stars changed their encounter.

leastWorthwhile.text: There was no particularly confusing or repetitive action in this brief chapter.

surprise.text: The result emphasized that matter once spread through colliding clouds now crosses as small, widely separated stars.

arbitrary.text: The combination had a clear purpose: the stars were approaching the returning galaxy's outskirts.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the contrast between the gas and stellar crossings made me curious about the shared galaxy's later history.
